findings.evidence:
Fast-create merging is enabled in the normal submit-to-job-table path: `pkg/ddl/executor.go:10127`-`pkg/ddl/executor.go:10138` calls `mergeCreateTableJobs` when `EnableFastCreateTable` is on.
The merged `ActionCreateTables` job rebuilds `InvolvingSchemaInfo` using only `{Database, Table}` entries and drops any shared-involving objects from the original `ActionCreateTable` jobs: `pkg/ddl/executor.go:3202`-`pkg/ddl/executor.go:3246`.
But individual create-table jobs can include shared-involving placement policies: `pkg/ddl/executor.go:2962`-`pkg/ddl/executor.go:3003` adds `{Policy: ..., Mode: SharedInvolving}`.
Job scheduler concurrency control relies on `InvolvingSchemaInfo`, and policy conflicts are only detected via `info.Policy`: `pkg/ddl/ddl_running_jobs.go:126`-`pkg/ddl/ddl_running_jobs.go:172`.
Drop placement policy jobs involve only the policy key and are pre-checked via InfoSchema (won’t see pending/merged create-table jobs): `pkg/ddl/executor.go:9496`-`pkg/ddl/executor.go:9529`.
Second confirmation (write-skew risk): create-table policy existence checks are snapshot reads without locking the policy key: `pkg/ddl/placement_policy.go:162`-`pkg/ddl/placement_policy.go:177`; drop-policy “not in use” checks are also InfoSchema/meta snapshot based: `pkg/ddl/placement_policy.go:343`-`pkg/ddl/placement_policy.go:366`.
findings.fix: When merging into `ActionCreateTables`, build `combinedJob.InvolvingSchemaInfo` as a union/dedup of all original jobs’ `GetInvolvingSchemaInfo()` (preserving `Mode`), not just newly-created `{Database, Table}` entries. This keeps shared objects (e.g. placement policies) in the merged job so the scheduler can serialize conflicts correctly.
findings.impact: With `tidb_enable_fast_create_table=ON`, two create-table statements that get merged into one `ActionCreateTables` job can lose shared-involving dependencies (notably placement policies). The scheduler may then run `DROP PLACEMENT POLICY p` concurrently with the merged create-tables job that still references `p`, enabling write-skew where the policy is dropped but the table(s) commit with a dangling `PlacementPolicyRef`, breaking metadata invariants and potentially leading to incorrect/failed placement rule handling and later DDL/infoschema issues.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (f0813a369666): the merge logic still rebuilds `InvolvingSchemaInfo` with only `{Database, Table}` in `upstream/master:pkg/ddl/job_submitter.go:207`-`upstream/master:pkg/ddl/job_submitter.go:247`, still omitting shared-involving policy entries from original create-table jobs.
findings.verify:
Add a unit test for `mergeCreateTableJobsOfSameSchema` ensuring policy/shared entries are preserved in the merged job’s `InvolvingSchemaInfo`.
Add an integration test: enable fast create; submit two `CREATE TABLE ... PLACEMENT POLICY p` concurrently to force merge, concurrently `DROP PLACEMENT POLICY p`; assert the drop is blocked/cancelled as “in use” and no table ends up referencing a non-existent policy.
findings.what: Merged `ActionCreateTables` jobs drop shared `InvolvingSchemaInfo` (e.g. placement policy refs), allowing the DDL scheduler to run conflicting policy DDL concurrently and potentially commit tables with dangling placement policy references.

subject: ddl: integrate fast create table into normal general DDL workflow (#55025)
summary: Reviewed this commit vs first parent, focusing on DDL metadata/state-machine impacts of integrating fast create table. Found a High-severity concurrency/metadata issue: the new create-table job merging path rebuilds `InvolvingSchemaInfo` incompletely, dropping shared dependencies (notably placement policies), which can let conflicting DDLs run concurrently and create inconsistent metadata; this is not fixed in later upstream history.
